decision.risk_area: security-sensitive code (csrf); public API contracts (accepts helper)
decision.why: Three independent bug fixes in different modules; the csrf and accepts changes touch risk-floor areas, so the whole task starts at deep; tests are present.
decision.shared:
Run the relevant tests with: npx vitest --run <test file paths>
Do not commit.

parts.title: CSRF middleware: skip OPTIONS requests
parts.text:
The csrf middleware rejects OPTIONS requests (for example CORS preflight)
when the Origin doesn't match. RFC 9110 defines OPTIONS as a safe method,
like GET and HEAD, so it should not be subject to CSRF validation.
parts.why: Change in the CSRF validation path, a security-sensitive area, so deep is the floor; the fix itself is small, so medium effort.

parts.title: ETag middleware: whitespace around If-None-Match commas
parts.text:
The etag middleware returns 200 with the full body instead of 304 when the
If-None-Match header has whitespace before a comma, e.g. `"a" , "b"`, even
though the current ETag is in the list. RFC 9110 allows optional whitespace
on both sides of the list delimiter.
parts.why: Ordinary bug with a clear reproduction and tests present; no risk-floor area is touched, so standard at its default effort.

parts.title: accepts() helper: subtype wildcard matching
parts.text:
The `accepts()` helper's default matcher ignores subtype wildcards sent by
clients. With supports ['application/json', 'text/html'], `Accept: application/*`
falls back to the default instead of returning application/json. A subtype
wildcard (`type/*`) should match a supported type of that type. At the same
quality value an exact match takes precedence over a wildcard match. The global
wildcards `*/*` and `*` keep their current behavior: they fall through to the
configured default rather than picking a supported value.
parts.risk_area: public API contracts (accepts helper behavior change)
parts.why: Changes matching semantics of an exported helper other users depend on, so it is a risk-floor area and deep; the rules are specified precisely.
